niche_preference_profile: This user prefers interfaces with strong visual styling rather than plain utility: rounded cards and pill buttons, clear hierarchy, and layouts that either feel compact and information-efficient or intentionally spacious when used to create a premium hero-focused presentation. They consistently like richer presentation elements such as imagery, gradients, overlay cards, and vivid accent color, while rejecting flat, boxy, overly segmented, or visually dull designs. Their color preference is mixed by context, but trends toward dark or mixed dark-light themes with controlled contrast, avoiding both harsh neon overload and bland monochrome minimalism.

top_7_criteria.description: Prefers softer, more rounded cards, modals, and especially pill-shaped buttons over squarer or flatter components.
Prefers interfaces with obvious hierarchy: prominent hero stats or titles, clear sectioning, aligned rows, and stronger emphasis on primary actions or key information.
Prefers visually rich UI treatment such as imagery, album art, photo thumbnails, gradients, shadows, overlay previews, and premium-looking cards rather than empty, plain, or low-energy surfaces.
Prefers bold accent-driven color systems and stronger contrast, often with dark or mixed dark-light themes, over flat all-light schemes or weakly differentiated palettes.

Prefers efficient information presentation with good content completeness and screen utilization, whether through compact dense layouts or simplified hero-focused summaries, as long as the hierarchy stays clear.
Prefers content organized into coherent grouped sections, integrated summary cards, or consistent list/grid structures rather than fragmented split panels or overly segmented boxed sub-sections.

Prefers buttons and controls that feel tangible and explicit, including filled secondary actions, larger full-width CTAs, and more prominent icon treatments rather than text-only or weak outline controls.
